pr_body:
Closes #5589 Edit: PR of non-ICU time_bucket function has been split into [#5835](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/5835). Implemented four overloads of ICU time_bucket function. They behave almost same as [TimescaleDB's time_bucket](https://docs.timescale.com/api/latest/hyperfunctions/time_bucket/). 
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMP)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMPTZ)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: DATE)

TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMP, offset: INTERVAL)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMPTZ, offset: INTERVAL)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: DATE, offset: INTERVAL)

TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMP, origin: TIMESTAMP)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMPTZ, origin: TIMESTAMPTZ)
TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: DATE, origin: DATE)

TIME_BUCKET(bucket_width: INTERVAL, ts: TIMESTAMPTZ, timezone: TEXT)
To ease the tests, I set the default origin to '2000-01-03 00:00:00+00' (when bucket_width is small) or '2000-01-01 00:00:00+00' (when bucket_width is large) as the same as TimescaleDB.

Thanks for all the hard work! This is coming along nicely, so please don't be discouraged. I'd highly recommend merging from master before your next push - there have been some broken CI bits.  Oh and thanks for fixing the formatting - I swear I thought it was included!

> `time_bucket` result of timestamp on the day DST ended gets greater than the original timestamp.

That's odd - I'm going to pull your code and step into it.

It looks like the problem is that there is a difference between the number of hours between the TB epoch and the non-DST times on the 29th (7203 == 300d 3h) and the interval that `DATE_SUB` computes using ICU's date subtraction logic (300h 4h).

There is a bug in the ICU TSTZ difference code. It is moving the start date forward instead of moving the end date backwards. So when it moves the epoch date forward by 300 days, it gains an hour crossing the spring DST boundary and never gives it back, resulting in an extra hour of difference at the next step. This is not symmetrical with the interval addition code.  I'll have a closer look tomorrow and hopefully have a fix.

Thanks for your investigation!

issue_context.title: Implement TIME_BUCKET Function
issue_context.body: `time_bucket` allows for truncation/bucketing by an arbitrary interval, instead of only by whole minutes, whole hours, etc. See e.g. the [Timescale docs](https://docs.timescale.com/api/latest/hyperfunctions/time_bucket/) or [Singlestore docs](https://docs.singlestore.com/managed-service/en/reference/sql-reference/time-series-functions/time_bucket.html).
comments: I would like to work on this.

review_comments: Are these changes used? I couldn't see where.

I don't use ConvertToString explicitly, but CI on Windows failed without DUCKDB_API specifiers.
https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/actions/runs/3722576787/jobs/6313517634#step:4:2383

I think this is not correct because with DST a day is not always 24 hours long!  For intervals less than days, you need to just use the basic µs delta `ts.value - origin.value`. But you also need a _third_ common routine for anything with days, and then you need the full interval value so you can do a kind of long division between the result of `Sub` and that interval.
Introduced a new routine for bucket_width that can be converted to days.
Now that you have split out the days, you don't need to do anything as complex as this to get `ts_micros`. You can just compute `ts.value` - `origin.value` (using the overflow detector).

When you are using sub-day intervals, then you don't need to worry about day boundaries. That's why I said you should split out a separate case for when there are days in the `interval_t`. That is also what ICU does if I am not mistaken, so that is the way the world works.

I'm surprised by the error in `Add` - ICU does have resolution issues with large values, but they are typically measured in millennia, not days. I'll try to have a look, but my time is becoming limited.  its a very simple repro though and should be filed as a separate issue.

> When you are using sub-day intervals, then you don't need to worry about day boundaries. 

`Interval::GetMicro` I used does not use ICU and treats the 23-hour or 25-hour DST boundary day as a 24-hour day.
So `int64_t ts_micros = Interval::GetMicro(Sub(calendar, ts, origin))` calculates with ±1 hour error when there is a DST boundary between `ts` and `origin`.
I don't need to worry about DST boundaries when getting epoch microseconds from `timestamp_t` directly without going through `interval_t`.

Yes and I think this is correct. After all, my date add fix shows that ICU does this in `Americas/Los_Angeles`:

```sql
set Calendar = 'gregorian';
set TimeZone = 'America/Los_Angeles';
select '1999-12-31 16:00:00-08'::timestamptz + interval 2400 hours
-- 2000-04-09 17:00:00-07
```

In other words, it adds 2400 hours, not 100 days. Which is what I would expect.
